title: City payments to nursing homes and to the companies they name as related
question: Has the City paid any nursing home in the State files, or any company a nursing home names as related to it, and what do those homes' reports show?
finding: 6 City payees carry the exact name of a nursing home or of a related company named in a home's report: $234.8 million in all. Crestwood Behavioral Health Inc (DPH, 2017 to 2027, $191.1 million); Helios Healthcare LLC (DPH, 2017 to 2027, $29.5 million); Sequoia Living (HOM, HSA, MYR, 2018 to 2027, $12.8 million); Garfield Nursing Home Inc (DPH, 2027, $581,859); Eden Healthcare Center (DPH, 2027, $468,450); Medical Hill Healthcare Center (DPH, 2027, $336,220).
how: The Controller's vendor payments, summed by payee, department and fiscal-year label, matched on the whole name after removing punctuation and endings such as LLC or Inc against: every California skilled-nursing home's name and legal name in the State reports, every related company the homes name, and the federal provider and legal business names. Names shorter than six letters are not matched; payees with less than $10,000 in all (refunds, fees) are left out.
limits: A name match is only a name match: two companies can share a name, and a City payment to a home is normally for care the City bought (placements of patients the City is responsible for). The fiscal-year label is the year the Controller files a payment under, not always the year it was made.
